cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I serve the birthday pudding, choose: Grandma first or the birthday child first? We have a custom for each.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put their plates together and serve them at once.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can put the plates together. I can't hand over one first slice twice. Which custom are we using?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal size still leaves one first cut. Please choose whose plate I put it on before I pick up the knife.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects simultaneous service and A5 equal size as insufficient to choose precedence, combining expertise with a governing-custom demand.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 simultaneous plates leads A3 first-slice distinction; B4 equal slices leads A5 first-cut distinction.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 offer reasonable practical compromises to avoid upsetting either diner.

heightening.evidence: A5 mostly repeats A3 firstness objection; the situation and response do not develop much after B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 Grandma, birthday child and pudding establish competing customs and serving task.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 is concise, but its first-cut wording repeats a semantic distinction rather than creating a new playable consequence.
